Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The human eye is like a camera; its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the retina.
False 1: The human eye is like a camera; its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the cornea.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Light enters the eye through a thin membrane called the cornea, which forms the transparent bulge on the front surface of the eyeball.
False 1: Light enters the eye through a thin membrane called the retina, which forms the transparent bulge on the front surface of the eyeball.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The eyeball is approximately spherical in shape with a diameter of about 2.3 cm.
False 1: The eyeball is approximately spherical in shape with a diameter of about 23 cm.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Most of the refraction for light rays entering the eye occurs at the outer surface of the cornea.
False 1: Most of the refraction for light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of the crystalline lens.
False 2: Most of the refraction for light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of the retina.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The crystalline lens provides the finer adjustment of focal length required to focus objects at different distances on the retina.
False 1: The cornea provides the finer adjustment of focal length required to focus objects at different distances on the retina.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil.
False 1: Iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the amount of light entering the eye directly.
False 2: Cornea is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye.
False 1: The iris regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye directly.
False 2: The pupil regulates and controls the focal length of the eye lens.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The eye lens forms an inverted real image of the object on the retina.
False 1: The eye lens forms an upright virtual image of the object on the retina.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Light-sensitive cells in the retina get activated upon illumination and generate electrical signals sent to the brain via the optic nerves.
False 1: Light-sensitive cells in the retina get activated upon illumination and generate chemical signals sent to the brain via the optic nerves.
False 2: Light-sensitive cells in the cornea get activated upon illumination and generate electrical signals sent to the brain via the optic nerves.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: When ciliary muscles are relaxed, the lens becomes thin and its focal length increases, enabling us to see distant objects clearly.
False 1: When ciliary muscles are relaxed, the lens becomes thick and its focal length decreases, enabling us to see distant objects clearly.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: When looking at nearby objects, the ciliary muscles contract, increasing the curvature of the eye lens, making it thicker and decreasing its focal length.
False 1: When looking at nearby objects, the ciliary muscles relax, increasing the curvature of the eye lens, making it thicker and decreasing its focal length.
False 2: When looking at nearby objects, the ciliary muscles contract, decreasing the curvature of the eye lens, making it thinner and increasing its focal length.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called accommodation.
False 1: The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called adaptation.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The minimum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain is called the least distance of distinct vision or the near point of the eye.
False 1: The maximum distance at which objects can be seen most distinctly without strain is called the least distance of distinct vision or the near point of the eye.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: For a young adult with normal vision, the near point is about 25 cm.
False 1: For a young adult with normal vision, the near point is about 25 m.
False 2: For a young adult with normal vision, the far point is about 25 cm.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The farthest point up to which the eye can see objects clearly is called the far point, which is infinity for a normal eye.
False 1: The nearest point up to which the eye can see objects clearly is called the far point, which is infinity for a normal eye.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Cataract is the condition where the crystalline lens becomes milky and cloudy at old age, causing partial or complete loss of vision.
False 1: Cataract is the condition where the retina becomes milky and cloudy at old age, causing partial or complete loss of vision.
False 2: Presbyopia is the condition where the crystalline lens becomes milky and cloudy at old age, causing partial or complete loss of vision.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Vision can be restored through cataract surgery.
False 1: Vision cannot be restored once cataract has developed.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Myopia is also known as near-sightedness; a person with myopia can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.
False 1: Myopia is also known as far-sightedness; a person with myopia can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.
False 2: Hypermetropia is also known as near-sightedness; a person with hypermetropia can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: In a myopic eye, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of at the retina.
False 1: In a myopic eye, the image of a distant object is formed behind the retina instead of at the retina.
False 2: In a hypermetropic eye, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of at the retina.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Myopia may arise due to excessive curvature of the eye lens or elongation of the eyeball.
False 1: Myopia may arise due to insufficient curvature of the eye lens or shortening of the eyeball.
False 2: Hypermetropia may arise due to excessive curvature of the eye lens or elongation of the eyeball.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Myopia is corrected by using a concave lens of suitable power.
False 1: Myopia is corrected by using a convex lens of suitable power.
False 2: Hypermetropia is corrected by using a concave lens of suitable power.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Hypermetropia is also known as far-sightedness; a person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.
False 1: Hypermetropia is also known as near-sightedness; a person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.
False 2: Myopia is also known as far-sightedness; a person with myopia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: In hypermetropia, light rays from a close object are focussed at a point behind the retina.
False 1: In hypermetropia, light rays from a close object are focussed at a point in front of the retina.
False 2: In myopia, light rays from a close object are focussed at a point behind the retina.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Hypermetropia arises because the focal length of the eye lens is too long or the eyeball has become too small.
False 1: Hypermetropia arises because the focal length of the eye lens is too short or the eyeball has become too large.
False 2: Myopia arises because the focal length of the eye lens is too long or the eyeball has become too small.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Hypermetropia is corrected by using a convex lens of appropriate power.
False 1: Hypermetropia is corrected by using a concave lens of appropriate power.
False 2: Myopia is corrected by using a convex lens of appropriate power.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Presbyopia arises due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens with ageing.
False 1: Presbyopia arises due to the gradual strengthening of the ciliary muscles and increasing flexibility of the eye lens with ageing.
False 2: Cataract arises due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens with ageing.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: A person suffering from both myopia and hypermetropia often requires bi-focal lenses with a concave upper portion (for distant vision) and a convex lower portion (for near vision).
False 1: A person suffering from both myopia and hypermetropia often requires bi-focal lenses with a convex upper portion (for distant vision) and a concave lower portion (for near vision).

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a glass prism is called dispersion; the band of colours is called a spectrum.
False 1: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a glass prism is called refraction; the band of colours is called a spectrum.
False 2: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a glass prism is called dispersion; the band of colours is called scattering.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The colours visible in the spectrum are Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange and Red (VIBGYOR).
False 1: The colours visible in the spectrum are Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Red and Orange (VIBGYRO).

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Red light bends the least while violet bends the most when passing through a prism.
False 1: Violet light bends the least while red bends the most when passing through a prism.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Isaac Newton was the first to use a glass prism to obtain the spectrum of sunlight.
False 1: Isaac Newton was the first to use a glass prism to obtain the spectrum of moonlight.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Newton placed a second identical prism in an inverted position, allowing all colours of the spectrum to pass through it; a beam of white light emerged from the other side, showing that sunlight is made up of seven colours.
False 1: Newton placed a second identical prism in the same position, allowing all colours of the spectrum to pass through it; a beam of white light emerged from the other side, showing that sunlight is made up of seven colours.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky after a rain shower, caused by dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets.
False 1: A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky after a rain shower, caused by dispersion of sunlight by dust particles.
False 2: A rainbow is a natural spectrum appearing in the sky before a rain shower, caused by dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: A rainbow is always formed in a direction opposite to that of the Sun.
False 1: A rainbow is always formed in the same direction as that of the Sun.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Water droplets act like small prisms: they refract and disperse sunlight, then reflect it internally, and finally refract it again when it comes out.
False 1: Water droplets act like small mirrors: they only reflect sunlight internally without any refraction or dispersion.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight, which changes continuously as the physical conditions of the atmosphere are not stationary.
False 1: The twinkling of a star is due to the star itself emitting light of varying intensity continuously.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Since stars are very distant, they approximate point-sized sources of light, which causes the twinkling effect.
False 1: Since stars are very distant, they appear as extended sources of light, which nullifies the twinkling effect.
False 2: Since planets are very distant, they approximate point-sized sources of light, which causes the twinkling effect.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Planets do not twinkle because they are seen as extended sources of light, so variations in light from all point-sized sources average out to zero.
False 1: Planets do not twinkle because they are point-sized sources of light, so their light does not undergo atmospheric refraction.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The Sun is visible about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and about 2 minutes after actual sunset due to atmospheric refraction.
False 1: The Sun is visible about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and about 2 minutes after actual sunset due to reflection of sunlight by clouds.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: The sky appears dark to passengers flying at very high altitudes as scattering is not prominent at such heights.
False 1: The sky appears darker blue to passengers flying at very high altitudes as scattering is more prominent at such heights.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Fine particles in the atmosphere scatter blue light (shorter wavelengths) more strongly than red light (longer wavelengths), making the sky appear blue.
False 1: Fine particles in the atmosphere scatter red light (longer wavelengths) more strongly than blue light (shorter wavelengths), making the sky appear blue.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Red light is least scattered by fog or smoke, which is why danger signal lights are red — they can be seen in the same colour at a distance.
False 1: Blue light is least scattered by fog or smoke, which is why danger signal lights are red — they can be seen in the same colour at a distance.

Chapter: 10th Ch10 - The Human Eye and the Colourful World
True Statement: Very fine particles scatter mainly blue light while particles of larger size scatter light of longer wavelengths.
False 1: Very fine particles scatter mainly red light while particles of larger size scatter light of shorter wavelengths.
